fields.h1: Build a Surgery Consent Form Signed Before the OR
fields.hero_description: Describe your surgical service. Emergent builds a surgery consent form that names the procedure and side, times each signature and lists cases still waiting.
fields.features_heading: What a Surgical Consent Record Holds
fields.features_subheading: The fields a chart needs before an operation, plus the checks your pre-op nurses run before the first case.
fields.feature_1:
The site and side, typed by the patient

Ask the patient to type the site and side of the operation without seeing the booking. An answer that does not match the schedule locks the signature and alerts the surgeon's office.
fields.feature_2:
One screen per risk statement

Give each risk your surgeon discusses its own screen, in the words the surgeon uses aloud. The patient confirms every statement, and the signature box opens only after the last one.
fields.feature_3:
A time on every signature

Set up the surgeon, the patient and any witness as separate signers. Each signature saves the date and the minute it was made, and the record shows the order they signed in.
fields.feature_4:
An unsigned-case check at a set hour

Pick the hour your team reviews tomorrow's cases. Each case without a signed form goes to the nurse you name, with the patient's phone number and the start time attached.
fields.feature_5:
Old consents kept, never overwritten

Send a new link when a case moves past your time limit or the planned procedure changes. The earlier form stays on the record, marked superseded, beside the one now in force.
fields.feature_6:
The source code, in your own repository

Export the full code to GitHub. A developer on your team can run the consent form inside your patient portal or scheduling system, then keep changing it there without starting over.
fields.why_title: Why Build Surgery Consent Forms on Emergent?
fields.why_description: A downloaded PDF holds a signature and little else. Emergent ties every signature to its time and to the case it covers.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Surgical Teams Run Consent
fields.tab_content_1:
The 6 p.m. check finds one unsigned case

Lakeview Surgery Center sends the consent link with the pre-op call, 3 days before surgery. At 6 p.m. the night before, the board lists tomorrow's 14 cases, and 13 have a signed consent. Dana Price's 7:30 a.m. case does not, and charge nurse Ruth Alvarez gets her phone number.
fields.tab_content_2:
Left or right, confirmed in the patient's words

Northwind Orthopedics books Ellen Ward for a right knee arthroscopy. Her consent form asks which knee is being operated on and never shows the booking. She types left. The signature stays locked, and Dr. Sam Okoye's office gets a task to call her before she signs anything.
fields.tab_content_3:
Three signatures with three times on the chart

Dr. Maya Lin explains the gallbladder removal and its alternatives to Tom Reyes on Riverside General's surgical unit. Tom signs at 9:38 a.m., nurse Grace Kim signs as witness at 9:39 a.m., and Dr. Lin signs at 9:42 a.m. His chart holds the form with all three times before he moves to pre-op holding.
fields.tab_content_4:
Past its 30 days, a consent goes back to the patient

Lakeview's own policy treats a consent signed more than 30 days before surgery as out of date. Marcus Bell's knee replacement moved to a later date, and by then his signed form will be 41 days old. He gets a new link that afternoon, and the old form stays on his record marked superseded.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Surgery Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Most of the work is agreeing on wording with your surgeons. Building the form comes last and takes the least time.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Collect the forms you use now
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Cover the elements a chart needs
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write risks in the surgeon's words
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Decide who signs and who witnesses
fields.howto_step_1_des: Gather the consent document each surgeon uses today, whether it lives in Word, on a printed pad or as a scanned page. Mark every place where two surgeons word the same thing differently. Settle those differences before anything gets built.
fields.howto_step_2_des: CMS guidance for hospitals lists a minimum: the hospital, the procedure, the responsible practitioner, a statement that the patient heard the risks and alternatives, and a signature with its date and time. Make each one a required field, not fine print.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask each surgeon for the risks they discuss for their common procedures, written the way they say them in clinic. Keep one statement per line. Short sentences read well on a phone, and each line gets its own confirmation from the patient.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List the signers for each type of case: the patient or a legal representative, the surgeon, and a witness when your policy asks for one. Give each signer a separate line with a role label and a field for the time.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your wording and your signer list into Emergent. It builds the form with the side check, timed signature fields and a table of every case. Ask for changes in plain English, such as a Spanish version or a separate screen for photography.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Link the form to your scheduling system through its API. Each booked case then gets a consent link and a row on the board. Choose the hour of the unsigned-case check and the nurse who hears about any case still waiting.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it, then send it for review
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run two test cases, one where the side matches the booking and one where it does not, then open both records. Have your medical director and a healthcare attorney read the wording before the first patient signs it.

claims_to_source: Hospital Conditions of Participation require a properly executed informed consent form in the patient's chart before surgery, except in emergencies (42 CFR 482.51(b)(2))

CMS interpretive guidance lists the minimum elements of a properly executed consent form: hospital, procedure, responsible practitioner, statement that benefits, risks and alternatives were explained, signature, and date and time signed; a witness signature is an optional addition

The provider obtaining consent explains the procedure and verifies understanding, signs after the patient, and a nurse may witness by verifying the patient's name, signature, the surgery and the provider
Valid informed consent needs capacity, adequate disclosure and voluntariness
The Department of Health model Consent Form 1 is titled patient agreement to investigation or treatment and holds the procedure, the health professional's statement and the patient's signature
With married parents, either parent generally has authority to consent for a minor; practices may seek both for surgery, and custody arrangements change this
